variant_desc: Single-stream Huffman decoder (per-iter chain: refill -> table lookup -> shift, ~5-7 cycle dep chain) -> 4 independent interleaved bitstreams + 4 disjoint output segments so the OoO core overlaps the chains (variant 2: seed=44, n_scale=1.5x)
source_citation: Yann Collet, zstd Huffman X4 4-stream decoder (2015); Fabian Giesen 'Reading bits in far too many ways' parts 1-3 (2023, https://fgiesen.wordpress.com)
novelty_rationale: Tests recognition that a single-stream Huffman/FSE decoder leaves the OoO core's ILP unused because every iteration is a hard dependence chain (refill -> table lookup -> shift). The fix is an input-format change: encode the source as 4 independent bitstreams so 4 chains run in parallel through the same scalar issue width. No compiler invents this -- it requires changing the data format (and the encoder), not just the decode loop. zstd's 4-stream mode is the textbook real-world instance.
